content: Hydrochlorothiazide, commonly referred to as a water pill, is prescribed to manage high blood pressure and fluid retention caused by various conditions, including heart disease. This medication works by prompting the kidneys to eliminate excess water and salt from the body through urine. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Hydrochlorothiazide is available in tablet and liquid forms, taken orally. It is typically taken once or twice daily. If prescribed once daily, it should be taken in the morning. If prescribed twice daily, doses should be taken in the morning and late afternoon to minimize nighttime urination. This medication should be taken with meals or a snack. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take hydrochlorothiazide exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. While this medication helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Hydrochlorothiazide may also be used to treat diabetes insipidus, certain electrolyte imbalances, and to prevent kidney stones in patients with elevated calcium levels in their blood. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Before taking hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, sulfa drugs, or any other drugs. Provide a list of all medications, supplements, and vitamins you are taking, as certain drugs may interact with hydrochlorothiazide. If you are taking cholestyramine or colestipol, take them at least one hour after hydrochlorothiazide. Inform your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or kidney, liver, thyroid, or parathyroid disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor immediately. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor right away. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking hydrochlorothiazide. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate drowsiness caused by this drug. Additionally, avoid unnecessary or prolonged sun exposure, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as hydrochlorothiazide may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Follow your doctor’s dietary instructions while taking this medication. Your doctor may recommend consuming potassium-rich foods, such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice, to maintain proper electrolyte balance. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Frequent urination is a common side effect that usually subsides after a few weeks of taking hydrochlorothiazide. Notify your doctor if you experience severe or persistent symptoms such as muscle weakness, dizziness, cramps, thirst, stomach pain, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, headache, or hair loss. If you experience serious side effects, such as a sore throat with fever, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe skin rash with peeling, or difficulty breathing or swallowing, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store hydrochlorothiazide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Do not allow the oral liquid form to freeze. Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular blood pressure monitoring and occasional blood tests. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
